memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses said to the Lord, "Pardon your servant, Lord. I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since you have spoken to your servant. I am slow of speech and tongue." The Lord said to him, "Who gave human beings their mouths? Who makes them deaf or mute? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Is it not I, the Lord?"" - Exodus 4:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses now names a real limitation. He is not a good speaker, and he knows it. This is not false modesty — it is an honest assessment of a genuine weakness.

God's answer is stunning. He does not deny the weakness. He does not promise to remove it. He simply asks: who made your mouth?

This is God claiming full sovereignty over how each of us is made — including our limitations. The stammer, the slowness, the thing you have always been embarrassed about, is not a manufacturing error that escaped God's notice.

This is a heavy truth, and we must hold it tenderly. It does not mean disability is trivial or that we should not seek help and healing. Jesus healed many. But it does mean that no one is disqualified from God's service by weakness. Paul learned that God's power is perfected in weakness (2 Cor 12:9), and he stopped asking for the thorn to be removed.

The God who made your mouth knows what He is doing when He asks you to speak.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What weakness have I been treating as a disqualification?
2. Can I honestly say I trust God with the way He made me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You made me and You know my limits better than I do. Use even my weakness for Your glory. Amen.
